title: Units of a formal power series ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $T$ an indeterminate and $f\in R[[T]]$ [def-weil-formal-power-series]. Then $f$ is a unit of $R[[T]]$ if and only if its constant coefficient $f(0)$ is a unit of $R$. In particular a power series in $1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$, for instance a polynomial $B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with $B(0)=1$ regarded as a power series [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series], is a unit of $\mathbf Z[[T]]$.

source.place: Ch. II §27, proof of Lemma 27.10, p. 158 ("Because $f(t)^{-1}\in1+t\cdot\mathbf Z_\ell[[t]]$": a power series with constant term 1 over $\mathbf Z_\ell$ is invertible with inverse of the same form)
